evidence.intree_statement: Class EquivalenceOfCategories {C D : Category} (F : C ⟶ D) := { quasi_inverse : D ⟶ C; equivalence_counit : F ◯ quasi_inverse ≈ Id[D]; equivalence_unit : Id[C] ≈ quasi_inverse ◯ F }.
Definition CategoryEquivalence (C D : Category) : Type := ∃ F : C ⟶ D, EquivalenceOfCategories F.   Notation "C ≃ D" := (CategoryEquivalence C D) (at level 91).

statement_record.book: An equivalence of categories consists of functors F : C → D and G : D → C together with natural isomorphisms η : id_C ≅ GF and ε : FG ≅ id_D; C ≃ D when such data exists, and F 'defines an equivalence' when it extends to one. No triangle identities are imposed (the adjoint form comes later, Proposition 4.3.5).
statement_record.intree: Class EquivalenceOfCategories {C D} (F : C ⟶ D) := { quasi_inverse : D ⟶ C; equivalence_counit : F ◯ quasi_inverse ≈ Id[D]; equivalence_unit : Id[C] ≈ quasi_inverse ◯ F }, bundled as CategoryEquivalence C D := ∃ F, EquivalenceOfCategories F with notation C ≃ D.

evidence.intree_statement: Class Full `(F : C ⟶ D) := { prefmap {x y} (g : F x ~> F y) : x ~> y; fmap_sur {x y} (g : F x ~> F y) : fmap[F] (prefmap g) ≈ g }.
Class Faithful `(F : C ⟶ D) := { fmap_inj {x y} (f g : x ~> y) : fmap[F] f ≈ fmap[F] g → f ≈ g }.
Class EssentiallySurjective {C D : Category} (F : C ⟶ D) := { eso_obj : D → C; eso_iso (d : D) : F (eso_obj d) ≅ d }.

statement_record.book: F : C → D is FULL if each action on hom-sets C(x,y) → D(Fx,Fy) is surjective; FAITHFUL if each is injective; ESSENTIALLY SURJECTIVE ON OBJECTS if every d ∈ D is isomorphic to Fc for some c ∈ C.
statement_record.intree: Full: a chosen section prefmap of fmap[F] with fmap_sur : fmap[F] (prefmap g) ≈ g for every g : F x ~> F y. Faithful: fmap_inj : fmap[F] f ≈ fmap[F] g → f ≈ g for parallel f, g : x ~> y. EssentiallySurjective: a chosen eso_obj : D → C with eso_iso (d) : F (eso_obj d) ≅ d.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same, in the library's constructive house style. Faithfulness is literally injectivity of the hom-map, with ≈ on hom-setoids in place of = (faithful setoid rephrasing). Fullness and essential surjectivity are stated in SPLIT (choice-carrying) form: instead of the propositions 'fmap is surjective' and 'there exists c with Fc ≅ d', the classes carry a chosen preimage morphism and a chosen preimage object with its witnessing isomorphism. Classically these are equivalent to Riehl's formulations (given AC); constructively the split form is the stronger datum, which is exactly why FF_ESO_Equivalence needs no choice axiom (Theory/Equivalence.v:101-118 discloses this design and cites the HoTT Book ch. 9 and Makkai's anafunctors). No functoriality is demanded of prefmap (Theory/Functor.v:326-330, issue #118), so nothing beyond a genuine preimage is required.

statement_record.book: Fullness and faithfulness are LOCAL conditions: faithfulness identifies f = g only for parallel morphisms with the same domain and codomain, and fullness only requires arrows k : Fx → Fy whose domain and codomain are already in the image to be hit; globally a faithful functor need not be injective on morphisms and a full functor need not be surjective on morphisms. A faithful functor injective on objects is an EMBEDDING and exhibits its domain as a subcategory; a full and faithful functor is FULLY FAITHFUL, and a fully faithful functor injective on objects is a FULL EMBEDDING, exhibiting the domain as a FULL SUBCATEGORY.
statement_record.intree: Full/Faithful are per-hom-set classes (Theory/Functor.v:331,342 — both quantified over a single pair x, y), the fully-faithful conjunction is used throughout and named at Theory/Functor.v:355 (FullyFaithful, with the reflects-isomorphisms consequence) and bundled at Instance/Cat.v:157 (Record Isomorphism_FullyFaithful with fields to_full/to_faithful/from_full/from_faithful); subcategories are Construction/Subcategory.v (Record Subcategory line 31, Sub line 50, Incl line 59) with fullness of a subcategory (line 69) proven to make the inclusion a full functor (line 74).

statement_record.book: A functor that defines an equivalence of categories is full, faithful and essentially surjective on objects; conversely, ASSUMING THE AXIOM OF CHOICE, any functor with these three properties defines an equivalence. The converse picks, for each d ∈ D, an object Gd and an isomorphism ε_d : FGd ≅ d, then uses full faithfulness plus Lemma 1.5.10 to define G on morphisms, prove functoriality, and produce η : id_C ≅ GF.
statement_record.intree: Both directions, as four theorems: FF_ESO_Equivalence (Full + Faithful + EssentiallySurjective → EquivalenceOfCategories F) and Equivalence_Full / Equivalence_Faithful / Equivalence_EssSurj (EquivalenceOfCategories F → each of the three properties). The quasi-inverse ff_eso_inverse is defined on objects by eso_obj and on morphisms exactly by Riehl's recipe, prefmap (from (eso_iso d') ∘ g ∘ to (eso_iso d)) — the conjugation of Lemma 1.5.10 followed by the chosen fmap-preimage.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same theorem, with the choice bookkeeping relocated rather than assumed. Riehl's converse needs AC to select (Gd, ε_d) for every d; the library's EssentiallySurjective already CARRIES that selection as data (eso_obj/eso_iso, Theory/Equivalence.v:141), so FF_ESO_Equivalence invokes no choice principle and is axiom-free — the header at Theory/Equivalence.v:101-118 states this explicitly and cites the HoTT Book and Makkai. Formally the in-tree implication has a stronger hypothesis (chosen preimages rather than mere existence) and is therefore weaker as an implication, but under AC the two hypotheses coincide, so no mathematical content is lost; the forward direction is unconditional and matches the book exactly. Riehl's proof-internal appeal to Lemma 1.5.10 is discharged inline (the conjugation formula appears literally in ff_eso_inverse's fmap and in ff_eso_unit_coherence, line 131) rather than as a cited lemma.

evidence.intree_statement: Lemma premon_square_from {a b c d : C} (i : a ≅ b) (j : c ≅ d) (f : a ~> c) (g : b ~> d) : g ∘ to i ≈ to j ∘ f → f ∘ from i ≈ from j ∘ g.   (* Declared inside Section Premonoidal, whose context is `Context {C : Category}` plus `Context `{@Binoidal C}`; neither the statement nor the proof mentions the Binoidal instance, so Coq discharges only C and this is a general-category lemma. Header at lines 167-170: 'Conjugating a commuting square by isomorphisms on both vertical edges: from g ∘ to i ≈ to j ∘ f we get f ∘ from i ≈ from j ∘ g ... this converts every to-direction naturality field into its from-direction form, so the inverse squares need not be part of the class data.' *)

statement_record.book: Given a morphism f : a → b and isomorphisms u : a ≅ a' and v : b ≅ b', there is a UNIQUE morphism f' : a' → b' making any one — equivalently all — of the four displayed squares (built from u or u⁻¹ and v or v⁻¹) commute; explicitly f' := v f u⁻¹. The equivalence of the four commutativity conditions is left to Exercise 1.5.iii.
statement_record.intree: premon_square_from (Structure/Premonoidal.v:171): for isomorphisms i : a ≅ b, j : c ≅ d and morphisms f : a ~> c, g : b ~> d, g ∘ to i ≈ to j ∘ f implies f ∘ from i ≈ from j ∘ g. Renaming i := u, j := v and g := f', this is: from the square f' ∘ u ≈ v ∘ f infer the square f ∘ u⁻¹ ≈ v⁻¹ ∘ f' — one of the implications among Riehl's four commutativity conditions, in an arbitrary category.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: only the second half of the lemma is touched, and only one of its implications. Riehl's 1.5.10 has two halves — (i) EXISTENCE AND UNIQUENESS of f' : a' → b', with the explicit formula f' = v f u⁻¹, and (ii) the equivalence of the four squares built from u/u⁻¹ and v/v⁻¹ (deferred to Exercise 1.5.iii). premon_square_from delivers exactly one implication of (ii). It states nothing about existence, nothing about uniqueness, and does not give the converse or the two mixed square forms. The transport FORMULA itself (to v ∘ f ∘ from u) is pervasive in-tree as an idiom inside other definitions — Theory/Functor.v:159 is the coherence field of Functor_Setoid, Theory/Equivalence/FullFaithful.v:71 is the morphism action of ff_eso_inverse, Theory/Equivalence.v:243 equivalence_unit_conjugate is the instance of it for a fixed equivalence's unit — but it is nowhere isolated as a lemma about one f and two arbitrary isomorphisms.

gap: (a) EXISTENCE is unstated: no in-tree lemma introduces f' := to v ∘ f ∘ from u as the morphism making the square commute; the composite occurs only inside other definitions (Theory/Functor.v:159, Theory/Equivalence/FullFaithful.v:71,125, Theory/Equivalence.v:243, Construction/Karoubi/Universal.v:284). (b) UNIQUENESS is unstated: the cancellation tooling exists (Theory/Isomorphism.v:264/275/286 iso_to_monic/iso_from_monic/iso_to_epic, and :301 comp_inverse_unique) but nothing concludes that f' is the unique such morphism, which is the load-bearing half for Theorem 1.5.9's construction of G on morphisms. (c) Only ONE of the four commutativity conditions is linked to another: premon_square_from gives to-form ⇒ from-form; the converse and the two mixed forms (u against v⁻¹, u⁻¹ against v) are not stated, so Exercise 1.5.iii is only a quarter covered. (d) PLACEMENT/DISCOVERABILITY: the one general-category counterpart lives in Structure/Premonoidal.v under a premonoidal-flavoured name inside a Binoidal section, so no consumer looking for an isomorphism-transport lemma will find it; the natural home is Theory/Isomorphism.v.
